### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.completion

### Question

![1746011805](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6eb7df31-e85e-44fd-9365-2d89b326bf6c)


See the picture above. The top part is my config, below is yours...

I think it can be solved [here](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/088d67751584e4168f35bca89bad70ada7ea4636/lua/mini/completion.lua#L1244):

```lua

-- local label_detail = (details.detail or '') ..  (details.description or '')
local label_detail = details.detail or ''
label_detail = label_detail .. ((label_detail ~= '') and ' ' or '') .. (details.description or '')
label_detail = snippet_clue .. ((snippet_clue ~= '' and label_detail ~= '') and ' ' or '') .. label_detail

```

Slightly related: [This](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/issues/1768) feature request...)

Would you allow a PR adding the space?

comment_data.body:
> See the picture above. The top part is my config, below is yours...

The current "no space" approach was taken [directly from 'nvim-cmp'](https://github.com/hrsh7th/nvim-cmp/blob/b5311ab3ed9c846b585c0c15b7559be131ec4be9/lua/cmp/entry.lua#L331-L337). And its roots are from [`completionItemLabelDetails`](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#completionItemLabelDetails) which includes "without any spacing" (between label and `detail`), so the same is reasonable to apply to between `detail` and `description`. 

> Would you allow a PR adding the space?

Sure, sounds good. But it should have the same type of symmetric condition as for between `snippet_clue` and `label_detail`.

reply_data.body:
Thanks for the information!

According to the link to [CompletionItemLabelDetails](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#completionItemLabelDetails), "without any spacing" applies to label and detail, where label is defined in [CompletionItem](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#completionItem). I assume that CompletionItem.label corresponds to [abbr](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/088d67751584e4168f35bca89bad70ada7ea4636/lua/mini/completion.lua#L1253)?

In that case, stock [blink.cmp](https://github.com/Saghen/blink.cmp/blob/f233029f79312d1028cbf168a8eef3182bac5a4f/lua/blink/cmp/config/completion/menu.lua#L90) renders according to spec.

Stock blink:

```rust
// blink default columns = { { 'kind_icon' }, { 'label', 'label_description', gap = 1 } },
// pseudo example:
kind_icon PhantomData<...>(use std:marker:PhantomData) gap PhantomData<unknown>>
```

When `CompletionItemLabelDetails.details` is appended to `CompletionItem.label`, as shown above, the parenthesis make more sense in my opinion...

We can close this question if you like. Otherwise, the best action is perhaps to change the formatting, appending `CompletionItemLabelDetails.details` to `CompletionItem.label`.

I would like to ask another question. When working with `mini.completion`, the `S` snippet indicator becomes redundant and slightly intrusive after a while. 
I [removed](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/52239614264cede6fdd6ba80470734487521f538/lua/ak/config/coding/mini_completion.lua#L98) the indicator. For me, it's good enough that mini.snippets shows symbols after the snippet is expanded. Would you consider a configuration option to change the snippet symbol, allowing an empty string?

reply_data.body:
> We can close this question if you like.

I've already said that adding a conditional space between `detail` and `description` sounds good.

> Otherwise, the best action is perhaps to change the formatting, appending `CompletionItemLabelDetails.details` to `CompletionItem.label`.

Although it is according to spec, unfortunately merging `details` to `abbr` is not a 100% solution with built-in popup-menu because it will affect how matching characters are visualized. Using `menu` seems to be a better, "more native" approach here.

> I would like to ask another question. When working with `mini.completion`, the `S` snippet indicator becomes redundant and slightly intrusive after a while.
> I [removed](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/52239614264cede6fdd6ba80470734487521f538/lua/ak/config/coding/mini_completion.lua#L98) the indicator. For me, it's good enough that mini.snippets shows symbols after the snippet is expanded. Would you consider a configuration option to change the snippet symbol, allowing an empty string?

I considered that initially, but decided to go with always showing `S` detail. Similar to how "traditional" completion engines use `~` suffix in label. The reason *some* visual clue is needed here is because the item behaves significantly different form regular items.

The main issue here is selecting an item (for example, with a quick single `<Tab>` / `<C-n>`) and simply continuing typing will expand the snippet. If the user is not aware of that, it breaks the typing workflow: either by starting a full snippet session (with 'mini.snippets' showing tabstops) or by adding extra characters and moving cursor (without showing tabstops).

The other issue is that a word that is shown during up/down navigation is not necessarily (and usually in fact is not) the one that will be inserted.

It would have been redundant if this type of behavior was only for completion candidates with "Snippet" kind, but unfortunately LSP spec allows "snippet insert text format" for any other kind. So I'd like that snippet clue to be always visible.

We can close this question if you like.

I've already said that adding a conditional space between detail and description sounds good.
